messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Hydrocodone and acetaminophen is a strong prescription combination pain medicine.
The medicine contains an opioid, hydrocodone.
The medicine also contains acetaminophen.
Acetaminophen is used to manage moderate to moderately severe pain.
The medicine is used when other pain treatments do not treat your pain well enough.
The medicine is also used when you cannot tolerate non-opioid pain medicines.
An opioid pain medicine that can put you at risk for overdose and death.
You are at risk for opioid addiction, abuse, and misuse that can lead to death.
This risk exists even if you take your dose correctly as prescribed.
Hydrocodone and acetaminophen is a Schedule II controlled substance.
All branded hydrocodone and acetaminophen (Norco, Vicodin, Lortab, Hycet, Lorcet, Verdrocet, Xodol, Zamicet) have been discontinued.
Generic hydrocodone and acetaminophen tablets and oral solution is still available.
Hydrocodone and acetaminophen first gained FDA approval on May 3, 1982.
Triples: [["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "is a", "strong prescription combination pain medicine"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "contains", "hydrocodone"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "contains", "acetaminophen"], ["acetaminophen", "used to manage", "moderate to moderately severe pain"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "used when", "other pain treatments do not treat your pain well enough"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "used when", "you cannot tolerate non-opioid pain medicines"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "has warning", "risk for overdose and death"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "has warning", "risk for opioid addiction, abuse, and misuse that can lead to death"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "has warning", "risk exists even if you take your dose correctly as prescribed"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "has controlled substance schedule", "Schedule II"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "has brand name", "Norco"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "has brand name", "Vicodin"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "has brand name", "Lortab"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "has brand name", "Hycet"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "has brand name", "Lorcet"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "has brand name", "Verdrocet"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "has brand name", "Xodol"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "has brand name", "Zamicet"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "has dosage form", "tablets"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "has dosage form", "oral solution"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "fda approval date", "May 3, 1982"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "has status", "discontinued for branded versions"], ["Hydrocodone and Acetaminophen", "has status", "available as generic tablets and oral solution"]]
Relations: ["contains", "fda approval date", "has brand name", "has controlled substance schedule", "has dosage form", "has status", "has warning", "is a", "used to manage", "used when"]
Answer:

completion:
contains: The subject drug includes or comprises the substance or component specified by the object entity.  
fda approval date: The subject drug received approval from the Food and Drug Administration on the date specified by the object entity.  
has brand name: The subject drug is marketed under the brand name specified by the object entity.  
has controlled substance schedule: The subject drug is classified under the controlled substance schedule specified by the object entity.  
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.  
has status: The subject drug has the status or availability specified by the object entity.  
has warning: The subject drug has a warning or caution related to the risk or condition specified by the object entity.  
is a: The subject entity is categorized or classified as the type of entity specified by the object entity.  
used to manage: The subject drug is used to manage or treat the medical condition specified by the object entity.  
used when: The subject drug is used in the situation or condition specified by the object entity.
